issues.description: Equality on FrameProcessor instances uses identity but isn't documented as an invariant
issues.detail: The suppression hinges on `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`. Without overridden __eq__ on FrameProcessor this is identity comparison, which is fine, but the invariant is undocumented. State explicitly that `service` is an identity reference to the originating processor; otherwise a future __eq__ override could silently suppress the wrong frame or fail to suppress.

issues.description: Holding a FrameProcessor reference inside a Frame couples frame lifetime to processor lifetime
issues.detail: Frames are normally plain data; embedding a live FrameProcessor reference creates a back-pointer that can outlive the switcher, complicate serialization, and confuse readers expecting frames to be values. A weakref, processor name, or stable id would preserve the targeting semantics without the coupling. At minimum, document why a strong reference is required.

issues.description: Loop invariant for the suppression rule is not stated in the comment
issues.detail: The new push_frame logic has two suppression branches but no stated invariant. A literate comment should read roughly: "After push_frame returns, downstream sees at most one ServiceMetadataFrame per switch, originating from the active service, and never sees a ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame addressed to that active service." Without that, future maintainers cannot verify changes preserve the property.

issues.description: Asymmetric handling: request for non-active service is forwarded downstream
issues.detail: If `frame.service != active_service`, the request frame falls through to be pushed downstream. That is presumably intentional (inactive services route via ParallelPipeline and consume it themselves), but the asymmetry deserves an explicit comment, plus a test case asserting a request targeted at the inactive service is not suppressed by the switcher. Otherwise the invariant is only implicit.

issues.description: Forward-reference string `"FrameProcessor"` should be a real import under TYPE_CHECKING
issues.detail: The field is typed `service: "FrameProcessor"` but no import is visible in the diff. A stringified forward reference with no corresponding import will resolve incorrectly under `get_type_hints` and is unreadable. Add `from pipecat.processors.frame_processor import FrameProcessor` under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` and keep the quoted annotation, or import directly.

issues.description: Dataclass with a non-default mandatory field after inherited defaults risks ordering issues
issues.detail: ControlFrame likely inherits from a dataclass chain with default-valued fields. Adding a mandatory `service` field on a subclass can raise `TypeError: non-default argument follows default argument` depending on the base. Verify, and if so use `field(default=...)` or `kw_only=True`. Tests pass today but this is fragile to base-class evolution.

review.summary: The rename and targeting change is small, local, and the algorithm is straightforward: a switcher consumes the request frame once the addressed service has handled it. The logic is correct under the unstated invariant that FrameProcessor equality is identity and that `service` holds a live reference to the originating processor — both should be made explicit. The main rigor gaps are (1) embedding a FrameProcessor reference inside a Frame couples data to live objects, (2) the loop/branch invariant is not stated in a literate comment, and (3) the forward-referenced type annotation has no visible import. UNDER-AUDITED in the literate-comment sense; algorithmically RIGOROUS. No P0s.
